commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

## What to build

A developer clones the new, empty v0 repository and runs `make` with no arguments. It prints every task target with a one-line description. Each target first checks the installed Bun version against the pinned one and stops with both versions and the install hint on a mismatch, then installs the locked packages when the package file or lockfile changed, then calls a package script.

The targets are dev, lint, typecheck, test, test-coverage, e2e, check (all checks in merge-loop order), fix, build and help. Lint runs Biome with its recommended and React rules over all code. Typecheck runs TypeScript 7 in strict mode with checked index access and no emit. Test runs `bun test` on four parallel workers with a 15-second default limit per test. Test-coverage runs each listed pure file's own test file alone with coverage on, keeps only that file's lines, and fails any listed pure file under 90% lines; a listed file with no own test file counts as 0% and the output names the missing test file. Every change to a project's map is one event appended to its decision log, and the map is a pure fold of that log, run on every read with its fold time recorded. The fold holds the latest title, why, body and links of each node.

`werk add` proposes a card, an option or a source as a ghost, with its parent in the same single event; it prints "proposed" and refuses `--status decided`. A ghost's words are frozen: a second add with the same id refuses. `werk link` and `werk unlink` add or remove one typed link (refines, depends_on, supported_by, alternative_to); a link on a ghost is held until both ends are real. `werk accept <id> --actor you` makes a ghost real, with its ghost refines parents and the ghost options, sources and excerpts it is supported_by; without `--actor you` it refuses. `werk discard` drops a ghost, its ghost descendants and its own excerpts, and drops a ghost source only when no remaining card cites it. A minimal `werk show` prints one node with its status, who, parent and links.

The map rules live in one pure module: one parent per card, no cycle, an option has only alternative_to, a depends_on needs a reason, a depends_on to an ancestor or descendant is refused, ghost words are frozen. A write checks all its events against the folded map and appends all or none, naming the rule it breaks. The fold applies the same check to each committed line; a bad line is set aside as a problem with its log position, and the lines after it still fold. Ghosts sit outside every derivation.

The fold derives the stale, paused, postponed and waiting marks and their traces, so every rule and view reads them from one place. A reopen with the reason invalidated (the default) or rejected, and an amend, mark the direct depends_on dependents and the direct refines children stale. A reopen with the reason postponed pauses every card reached over refines children and depends_on dependents that existed at that moment, at any distance; the postponed card itself carries the postponed mark and stays open. ## What to build

`werk serve [--port]` starts one server process. The server holds one context per project (map, and later conversations, agents and builds); this ticket opens one context for the project it starts in, so a later project list adds contexts without reshaping the server. The project's store location can be set through the environment, which tests use.

Each project store has one lock file, taken by an exclusive create that fails when the file exists. A start that loses reads the lock: a dead pid is stale and is replaced; a live pid makes the start poll until the wait ends, then refuse with a message naming the pid and port; a lock that does not parse counts as held during the wait and stale after it. The server makes a random token at start and puts it in the page it serves. Every request that writes or starts anything must carry it, and every request whose Host is not a loopback name is refused. The token never goes into a log or into an agent's environment. Read requests need no token.

The map API is card-scoped: one read returns one card with its body, why, status, marks, rollup and its neighbours' ids and titles; one read returns the shape of the whole map (ids, kinds, statuses, edges, rollups) with no bodies. The server watches each project's log directory and starts the watch before it accepts connections. When the log grows, it sends a bare changed signal with no data on the live channel to every open page; the page then reads again.
